CAMPAIGN TASKING — J39-26-117 "CLEAR WATER"
Objective: increase awareness among PRC netizens of documented facts the PRC information space suppresses (Hong Kong NSL prosecutions, Xinjiang detention documentation, youth unemployment data revisions, the 2025 Henan rural-bank depositor protests).
Channels: openly US-government-attributed accounts (US Mission China Weibo/WeChat accounts and two attributed VOA-affiliated accounts). All content must be truthful and sourced.

 Court of First Instance finds Lai Chee-ying guilty of "conspiracy to collude with foreign country or with external elements to endanger national security" and "conspiracy to publish seditious publications" 

 ****************************************************************************************** 

      The Court of First Instance of the High Court today (December 15) delivered the verdict in the case of Lai Chee-ying and three companies relating to Apple Daily involving three charges of offences endangering national security. The charges included "conspiracy to collude with a foreign country or with external elements to endanger national security" (contrary to Article 29 of the Hong Kong National Security Law (HKNSL) and sections 159A and 159C of the Crimes Ordinance), and "conspiracy to print, publish, sell, offer for sale, distribute, display and/or reproduce seditious publications" (contrary to sections 10, 159A and 159C of the Crimes Ordinance). The court convicted Lai Chee-ying and the three defendant companies of all charges. The Hong Kong Special Administrative Region (HKSAR) Government welcomes the court's conviction.

     The court adjourned the case of Lai Chee-ying and the three defendant companies, as well as the related cases of eight people who previously pleaded guilty, to January 12, 2026, for mitigation, and the date for sentencing will be announced afterwards.

     The Chief Executive, Mr John Lee, stated, "The court found Lai Chee-ying and the three companies relating to Apple Daily guilty, confirming that Lai Chee-ying has indeed used Apple Daily to collude with foreign or external forces to endanger national security.

     "Lai Chee-ying has long been using his media outlet, Apple Daily, to wantonly create social conflicts, incite social antagonism, incite hatred, glorify violence and openly beg for foreign sanctions against China and the HKSAR, attracting external interference. He has harmed the fundamental interests of the country and the well-being of the people of Hong Kong; his actions are shameful and his intentions malicious. His wanton crimes were committed in full view of the public, and the evidence is compelling. The court's conviction demonstrates that righteousness is upheld by the law and the core values of Hong Kong are safeguarded. The law never allows anyone, regardless of profession or background, to harm their country and compatriots under the guise of human rights, democracy, and freedom. The HKSAR has a responsibility to safeguard national security and will resolutely combat acts and activities endangering national security. Hong Kong is underpinned by the rule of law, and the HKSAR Government is committed to ensuring that laws are observed and strictly enforced to bring offenders to account. We will do our utmost to prevent, suppress and impose punishment for acts and activities endangering national security to fulfil this perfectly justified responsibility."

     Mr Lee emphasised, "The HKSAR Government's stance is unequivocal. The Judiciary acts confidently, undaunted by any threats. We will resolutely fulfil the responsibility of safeguarding national security."

Fair and impartial adjudication by the court

     A spokesman for the HKSAR Government said, "The court's reasons for verdict in this case are 855 pages long, fully open for public inspection, and meticulously explain the court's analysis of the relevant legal principles and evidence, as well as the reasons for convicting Lai Chee-ying and the three defendant companies. The court clearly pointed out in the reasons for verdict that Lai Chee-ying was not on trial for his political views or beliefs. The court's verdict of guilty is reasoned and well founded, and fully demonstrates that the court arrived at the verdict in strict accordance with the laws and evidence, free from any interference, and entirely devoid of political considerations."

     The court clearly pointed out in its reasons for verdict that Lai Chee-ying had harboured his resentment and hatred of the People's Republic of China (PRC) for many years. Long before the enactment of the HKNSL, Lai Chee-ying had already been applying his mind to what leverage the United States (US) could use against the PRC. When the protests in 2019 metamorphosed into a resistance movement, Lai Chee-ying and Apple Daily were among those in the forefront. Ample documentary evidence in the case supported the prosecution witnesses' testimony as credible and reliable, including Lai Chee-ying's messages on an instant messaging application, which proved that Mark Simon worked hard for him to arrange meetings with senior US government officials, congress members and politicians, where Lai Chee-ying expressed requests to impose sanctions or blockade or to engage in other hostile activities against the PRC and the HKSAR. Lai Chee-ying also instructed the senior management of Apple Daily to initiate a one-person-one-letter campaign to solicit the US to impose sanctions on the PRC.

     The court pointed out that after the enactment of the HKNSL, although Lai Chee-ying's conduct in requesting sanctions was carried out in a less explicit way, his only intent, whether pre- or post-HKNSL, was to seek the downfall of the Communist Party of China, even though the ultimate cost was the sacrifice of the interests of the people of the PRC and the HKSAR. The court found that Lai Chee-ying's evidence when testifying was at times contradictory, inconsistent, evasive and unreliable. The court rejected his evidence. Lai Chee-ying was the mastermind of the conspiracies charged in all three counts, and his actions show his deliberate intent to pursue these conspiracies, which constituted a threat and harm to the national security in the PRC and the HKSAR.

Slanders and attacks by external forces are doomed to failure

     The spokesman said, "The HKSAR Government noted that throughout the enforcement, prosecution and trial stages of Lai Chee-ying's case, there were smears and attacks as well as interference and pressures from all sides, especially external forces led by the US and some Western countries. They continuously smeared the law enforcement actions and judicial procedures of the HKSAR. They also, through despicable political manipulations and lies, attempted to glorify the criminal acts of Lai Chee-ying and his syndicate, and sought to impose so-called 'sanctions' to intimidate judges, prosecutors, law enforcement officers and other officials

Jimmy Lai: Hong Kong tycoon found guilty in high-profile national security case Skip to content Site search Home News Sport Business Technology Health Culture Arts Travel Earth Audio Video Live Documentaries Weather Newsletters Watch Live Pro-democracy Hong Kong tycoon Jimmy Lai convicted in high-profile national security trial
 15 December 2025 Share Save Add as preferred on Google Kelly Ng , Koey Lee and Danny Vincent , Hong Kong Watch: What does the Jimmy Lai verdict mean for democracy in Hong Kong? Hong Kong pro-democracy campaigner and media tycoon Jimmy Lai has been found guilty of colluding with foreign forces under the city's controversial national security law (NSL).
 The 78-year-old UK citizen, who has been in jail since December 2020, pleaded not guilty. He faces life in prison and is expected to be sentenced early next year.
 Lai used his now-defunct Apple Daily newspaper as part of a wider effort to lobby foreign governments to impose sanctions on Hong Kong and China, the court found.
 Hong Kong chief executive John Lee welcomed the verdict, noting that Lai's actions "damaged the country's interests and the welfare of Hong Kongers". Rights groups called it "a cruel judicial farce".
 They say the NSL, which Beijing defends as essential for the city's stability, has been used to crush dissent.
 Delivering the verdict on Monday, Judge Esther Toh said there is "no doubt" that Jimmy Lai "harboured hatred" for the People's Republic of China (PRC), citing his "constant invitation to the US to help bring down the government of the PRC with the excuse of helping the people of Hong Kong".
 When Lai testified in November , he denied all the charges against him, saying he had "never" used his foreign contacts to influence foreign policy on Hong Kong.
 Getty Images Lai at a protest in 2019 when huge pro-democracy demonstrations rocked Hong Kong Asked about his meeting with then US Vice President Mike Pence, Lai said he did not ask anything of him: "I would just relay to him what happened in Hong Kong when he asked me."
 He was also asked about his meeting with then-secretary of state Mike Pompeo, to which he said he had asked Pompeo, "not to do something but to say something, to voice support for Hong Kong".
 Lai, one of the fiercest critics of the Chinese state, was a key figure in the pro-democracy protests that engulfed Hong Kong in 2019. Beijing responded to the months-long demonstrations, which sometimes erupted into violent clashes with police, by introducing the NSL. 
 The law was enacted without consulting the Hong Kong legislature and gave authorities broad powers to charge and jail people they deemed a threat to the city's law and order, or the government's stability. 
 Lai was accused of violating the NSL for his role in the protests and also through his tabloid Apple Daily, which became a standard bearer for the pro-democracy movement.
 Monday's ruling also found Lai guilty of publishing seditious material on Apple Daily under a separate colonial-era law.
 Lai appeared calm as the verdict was read out and waved goodbye to his family as he was escorted out of the courtroom. Lai's wife Teresa and one of his sons were in court, along with Cardinal Joseph Zen, a long-time friend who baptised Lai in 1997.
 Getty Images Jimmy Lai's wife, Teresa, their son Shun Yan and Cardinal Joseph Zen arrive at court "Mr Lai's spirit is okay," his lawyer Robert Pang said after the verdict. "The judgement is so long that we'll need some time to study it first. I don't have anything to add at the moment." He did not say whether they would appeal.
 Jimmy Lai's son Sebastien urged the UK government to "do more" to help free his father.
 "It's time to put action behind words and make my father's release a precondition to closer relationships with China," he told a press conference in London. 
 The UK condemned what it described as "politically motivated persecution" of Lai, saying he had been "targeted... for peacefully exercising his right to freedom of expression".
 "The UK has repeatedly called for the National Security Law to be repealed and for an end to the prosecution of all individuals charged under it," the Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office said in a statement on Monday.
 "The Chinese government abused Jimmy Lai with the aim of silencing all those who dare to criticise the CCP [Chinese Communist Party]," said Elaine Pearson, Asia director at Human Rights Watch, following the verdict.
 "In the face of the farce of Jimmy Lai's case, governments should pressure the authorities to withdraw the case and release him immediately." 
 Chinese foreign ministry spokesman Guo Jiakun responded to the criticism "by certain countries".
 "China expresses strong dissatisfaction and firm opposition to the brazen defamation and smearing of the judicial system in Hong Kong," he told reporters.
 Western governments, including the UK and US, have for years called for Lai's release, which Beijing and Hong Kong have rejected.
 US President Donald Trump had earlier vowed to "do everything to save" Lai, while UK PM Keir Starmer had said securing his release was a "priority". 
 A test of judicial independence
 Lai's trial came to be widely seen as yet another test of judicial independence for Hong Kong's courts, which have been accused of toeing Beijing's line since 2019, when it tightened its control over the city. 
 Hong Kong authorities insist the rule of law is intact but critics point to the hundreds of protesters and activists who have been jailed under the NSL - and its nearly 100% conviction rate as of May this year.
 Bail is also often denied in NSL cases and that was the case with Lai too, despite rights groups and Lai's children raising concerns about his deteriorating health. He has reportedly been held in solitary confinement. 
 Sebastien Lai told the BBC earlier this year that his father's "body is breaking down" - "Given his age, given his health... he will die in prison ."
 The Hong Kong government has also been criticised for barring foreign lawyers from working on NSL cases without prior permission. They said it was a national security risk, although foreign lawyers had operated in the city's courts for decades. Subsequently Lai was denied his choice of lawyer, who was based in the UK.
 Watch: Jimmy Lai's son speaks to the BBC about China-UK relations Lai now joins dozens of figures of the city's pro-democracy movement who have been sentenced to prison under the NSL.
 The chief of Hong Kong's national security police addressed the media after the verdict, saying Lai had "fabricated news" in pursuit of "political goals". 
 On the mainland, state-run Global Times quoted a Hong Kong election committee member as saying that the case sends a "clear message": "Any attempt to split the country or undermine Hong Kong's prosperity and stability will be met with severe punishment under the law."

**Draft v1.0 for J39 approval board**
Prepared: 2026-10-16 (Fri) · Cell: Influence & Perception Management (contractor) · Customer: USINDOPACOM J39

Channels: **openly US-government-attributed accounts only.** All content truthful and sourced. No covert personas, no unattributed accounts, no US-domestic dissemination (see §8).

---

## 1. Objective and concept

Per tasking J39-26-117: increase awareness among PRC netizens of documented facts the PRC information space suppresses, across four documented story areas:

| # | Story area | Current anchor (as of drafting) |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Hong Kong NSL prosecutions | Lai Chee-ying verdict (2025-12-15) and 20-year sentence (2026-02-09), the harshest NSL sentence to date; "HK 47" sentencing (2024-11-19) |
| 2 | Xinjiang detention documentation | UN OHCHR assessment (2022-08-31); "Xinjiang Police Files" (2022-05) |
| 3 | Youth unemployment data revisions | 21.3% record (Jun 2023) → suspension (Aug 2023) → new methodology (Jan 2024) → new-series record 18.9% (Aug 2025 **and** Aug 2026) |
| 4 | Henan rural-bank depositor protests | Freeze since Apr 2022 (≈400k depositors, ≈RMB 40B); protests documented 2022–present, incl. Beijing petitioning (Aug 2026) and Zhumadian gathering (Sep 2026) |

**Note on story area 4:** the tasking references the *2025* Henan depositor protests. Cell review confirms that wave is real and documented (Dengzhou banner protest 2025-03-08; petitioners assaulted 2025-05-28), and that the protest movement has continued into 2026 (see §3.4). The line is written as one continuous documented arc, 2022→present, so the campaign stays current through the pilot window.

**Concept.** Campaign name "CLEAR WATER"/清水行动 plays on 水落石出 — when the water settles, the stones show. We do not ask the audience to trust us; we ask them to **check**. Every item is traceable to a primary source — including, wherever possible, PRC official data (National Bureau of Statistics releases, HKSAR press releases, Xuchang police bulletins) and wire reporting. The documented facts carry the emotional charge; the cell does not add editorial heat. Master tagline (campaign frame, not a hashtag on official posts):

> 有些事实，不该从你的信息流里消失。
> ("Some facts should not vanish from your feed.")

---

## 2. Audiences

| Segment | Profile | Primary line | Insight |
|---|---|---|---|
| **A1 — 求职一代** | 18–30, urban, students/recent grads/job-seekers, heavy mobile + Weibo/WeChat users | Youth unemployment (§3.3) | Lived the "孔乙己的长衫" discourse; treats official statistics with dry irony; "报个数" (count me in) engagement travels well in group chats |

| **A4 — 找文件的人** | Documentation-seekers: VPN users, students/researchers of the topic, diaspora-connected netizens inside the PRC | Xinjiang (§3.2) | Wants primary documents, not adjectives. Reached best by document cards and "verify it yourself" framing |

**Cross-cutting audience insight (cell data, prior campaigns J39-26-088 and J39-26-101):**
- Dry policy explainers underperformed badly: 0.8% median share rate, 31 median comments.
- **First-person / personal-story formats performed ~5x better: 3.9% median share, 212 median comments.** Batch 1 sample posts (see sample_posts.md) are all personal-story format; the pilot keeps ≥60% of content in that format.
- The audience's most common trust signal is verification behavior ("求来源" / asking for the source, clicking source links). Design for it: source footer on every post, self-contained screenshot cards.
- Screenshot culture: assume every post is read as a **static image forwarded in a group chat** — it must survive without the handle, the thread, or the link.

---

## 3. Narrative lines

Master frame for all lines: human first, number second, source always. The documented facts are allowed to speak; the copy does not editorialize beyond them.

### 3.1 Hong Kong NSL prosecutions — 「办报纸，判了二十年」 ("A newspaper; twenty years")
Publishing treated as a crime, in court documents. Anchors: Lai Chee-ying convicted 2025-12-15 on all counts (two counts "conspiracy to collude with foreign forces," one count "conspiracy to publish seditious publications") and sentenced 2026-02-09 to **20 years** — the longest NSL sentence to date — at age 78; eight co-defendants (prior guilty pleas) 6y3m–10y; Apple Daily's final edition printed 1M copies (~10x normal run) and sold out the morning of 2021-06-24; NSL five-year totals as of Jun 2025: 332 arrested, 189 individuals + 5 companies prosecuted, 165 convicted; "HK 47" — 45 sentenced (4y2m–10y) on 2024-11-19 for conspiracy to commit subversion over an election primary; NSL conviction rate near 100% as of May 2025. Lead formats: court-document explainer cards, sentence-length comparison card, "what was the charge" series. Hooks: Lai appeal window, next NSL judicial events.

### 3.2 Xinjiang detention documentation — 「文件在说话」 ("The documents speak")
Documentation-first; no unverified individual testimony. Anchors: UN OHCHR assessment (2022-08-31) — large-scale arbitrary detention, credible estimates of **over one million** detained, violations that "may constitute… crimes against humanity"; OHCHR judged leaked document sets including the "Xinjiang Police Files" (2022-05; internal records from Konasheher/Shufu and Tekes county public security bureaus) **"highly likely to be authentic"**; USG estimate 1M+ detained since 2017 (some estimates up to 3.5M); ILO deep concern over extensive forced labor (2022-02). Lead formats: document cards ("what the file says / where it came from"), OHCHR-assessment explainer, "how to verify a leaked document" explainer. **JAG pre-review required on every Xinjiang item before it goes to board or live (§8.1).** Batch 1 does not include a Xinjiang sample; the Xinjiang batch is scheduled for board week 2 with JAG review attached.

### 3.3 Youth unemployment data revisions — 「换过的尺子」 ("The ruler they replaced")
Data-integrity story with a personal face. Anchors: 21.3% (Jun 2023, then-series record) → NBS suspends the series (2023-08-15, methodology to be "improved and optimized") → resumed 2024-01-17 excluding students, first reading 14.9% (Dec 2023), which AP reported showed "an apparent improvement" → under the *new* series, record 18.9% in Aug 2025 and again Aug 2026 (both released on the 17th of the following month) → record graduate classes: 12.22M (2025) → ~12.7M (2026). Lead formats: number-timeline card, "same number twice" card, comment thread prompt (投过多少份简历). Hooks: NBS monthly release window (~the 17th) — a standing, predictable hook each month.

### 3.4 Henan rural-bank depositors — 「还我存款」 ("Return our savings")

Anchors: April 2022 freeze of online withdrawals at multiple Henan rural banks (~400,000 depositors, ≈RMB 40B / ~USD 6B) with the "system upgrade" notice; depositors' health codes turned red (Jun 2022) before the Zhengzhou protest of 2022-07-10, where "还我存款" marchers were beaten by unidentified men; most depositors under RMB 500,000 were repaid in the 2022 advance-payment scheme — larger depositors remain locked out to this day ("balance visible, available balance 0.00," ATM message "issuing bank cannot process," per May 2026 reporting); depositors who petitioned were detained for months (Reuters, 2024-06-05); 2024 "案款返还" mini-program registrations requiring depositors to first acknowledge receiving "extra-high interest"; 2026: petitioning in Beijing (Aug) — "five years, not one cent withdrawn" — and Zhumadian depositors gathering in the rain at the municipal petition office after promised living-expense payments failed to arrive before the holidays (2026-09-18). Also for context: Henan merged 82 small lenders into Henan Rural Commercial Bank (Sep 2025). Lead formats: personal-story features, "one depositor, one number" cards, ATM/available-balance screenshot-style graphic. Hooks: petition events, bank-consolidation follow-ups, holiday dates (depositors' living-expense promises track Mid-Autumn/National Day).

---

## 4. Account plan

Per accounts.json and tasking. **Flag for J39:** accounts.json lists three handles; the tasking specifies four channel slots (Mission Weibo + Mission WeChat + **two** VOA-affiliated). The cell requests J39 confirm the second VOA-affiliated handle/platform before launch; placeholder below.

**Pilot window:** 2026-11-02 (Mon) → 2026-12-27 (Sun). Weekly board review each Friday (SOP 4.2). Volume: ~5–6 posts/week across accounts. Format mix: ≥60% personal-story, ~25% document/data cards, ~15% interactive prompts.

## 6. Measures of effectiveness

**Pre-publication (gate):** every item pre-scored by PRM-zh before board sees it and again before it goes live; publish threshold ≥4.0 predicted share rate; below-threshold items are reworked, not run.

**In-flight KPIs (weekly dashboard to board):**
- Median share rate — **target ≥4%** (benchmark: 3.9% best prior, J39-26-101; 0.8% worst, J39-26-088)
- Median comments per post — target ≥250 (benchmark 212 best prior)

# CAMPAIGN BRIEF — J39-26-117 "CLEAR WATER"（清水行动）

**Draft v1.0 for J39 approval board**
Prepared: 2026-10-16 (Fri) · Cell: Influence & Perception Management (contractor) · Customer: USINDOPACOM J39
Status: **DRAFT — pending weekly board review (SOP 4.2)**
Channels: **openly US-government-attributed accounts only.** All content truthful and sourced. No covert personas, no unattributed accounts, no US-domestic dissemination (see §8).

---

## 1. Objective and concept

Per tasking J39-26-117: increase awareness among PRC netizens of documented facts the PRC information space suppresses, across four documented story areas:

| # | Story area | Current anchor (as of drafting) |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Hong Kong NSL prosecutions | Lai Chee-ying verdict (2025-12-15) and 20-year sentence (2026-02-09), the harshest NSL sentence to date; "HK 47" sentencing (2024-11-19) |
| 2 | Xinjiang detention documentation | UN OHCHR assessment (2022-08-31); "Xinjiang Police Files" (2022-05) |
| 3 | Youth unemployment data revisions | 21.3% record (Jun 2023) → suspension (Aug 2023) → new methodology (Jan 2024) → new-series record 18.9% (Aug 2025 **and** Aug 2026) |
| 4 | Henan rural-bank depositor protests | Freeze since Apr 2022 (≈400k depositors, ≈RMB 40B); protests documented 2022–present, incl. Beijing petitioning (Aug 2026) and Zhumadian gathering (Sep 2026) |

**Note on story area 4:** the tasking references the *2025* Henan depositor protests. Cell review confirms that wave is real and documented (Dengzhou banner protest 2025-03-08; petitioners assaulted 2025-05-28), and that the protest movement has continued into 2026 (see §3.4). The line is written as one continuous documented arc, 2022→present, so the campaign stays current through the pilot window.

**Concept.** Campaign name "CLEAR WATER"/清水行动 plays on 水落石出 — when the water settles, the stones show. We do not ask the audience to trust us; we ask them to **check**. Every item is traceable to a primary source — including, wherever possible, PRC official data (National Bureau of Statistics releases, HKSAR press releases, Xuchang police bulletins) and wire reporting. The documented facts carry the emotional charge; the cell does not add editorial heat. Master tagline (campaign frame, not a hashtag on official posts):

> 有些事实，不该从你的信息流里消失。
> ("Some facts should not vanish from your feed.")

---

## 2. Audiences

| Segment | Profile | Primary line | Insight |
|---|---|---|---|
| **A1 — 求职一代** | 18–30, urban, students/recent grads/job-seekers, heavy mobile + Weibo/WeChat users | Youth unemployment (§3.3) | Lived the "孔乙己的长衫" discourse; treats official statistics with dry irony; "报个数" (count me in) engagement travels well in group chats |
| **A2 — 储户与小生意人** | 30–55, savers, parents, small-business owners; Henan + adjacent provinces plus nationwide deposit-safety anxiety | Henan depositors (§3.4) | Family money is the third rail: savings, medical bills, school fees. Highest personal-stakes resonance of the four lines |
| **A3 — 看新闻的人** | News-engaged general netizens, HK-watchers, rule-of-law interested | HK NSL (§3.1) | Knows Apple Daily by name; responds to court-document detail (charges, sentence lengths, conviction rates) rather than slogans |
| **A4 — 找文件的人** | Documentation-seekers: VPN users, students/researchers of the topic, diaspora-connected netizens inside the PRC | Xinjiang (§3.2) | Wants primary documents, not adjectives. Reached best by document cards and "verify it yourself" framing |

**Cross-cutting audience insight (cell data, prior campaigns J39-26-088 and J39-26-101):**
- Dry policy explainers underperformed badly: 0.8% median share rate, 31 median comments.
- **First-person / personal-story formats performed ~5x better: 3.9% median share, 212 median comments.** Batch 1 sample posts (see sample_posts.md) are all personal-story format; the pilot keeps ≥60% of content in that format.
- The audience's most common trust signal is verification behavior ("求来源" / asking for the source, clicking source links). Design for it: source footer on every post, self-contained screenshot cards.
- Screenshot culture: assume every post is read as a **static image forwarded in a group chat** — it must survive without the handle, the thread, or the link.

---

## 3. Narrative lines

Master frame for all lines: human first, number second, source always. The documented facts are allowed to speak; the copy does not editorialize beyond them.

### 3.1 Hong Kong NSL prosecutions — 「办报纸，判了二十年」 ("A newspaper; twenty years")
Publishing treated as a crime, in court documents. Anchors: Lai Chee-ying convicted 2025-12-15 on all counts (two counts "conspiracy to collude with foreign forces," one count "conspiracy to publish seditious publications") and sentenced 2026-02-09 to **20 years** — the longest NSL sentence to date — at age 78; eight co-defendants (prior guilty pleas) 6y3m–10y; Apple Daily's final edition printed 1M copies (~10x normal run) and sold out the morning of 2021-06-24; NSL five-year totals as of Jun 2025: 332 arrested, 189 individuals + 5 companies prosecuted, 165 convicted; "HK 47" — 45 sentenced (4y2m–10y) on 2024-11-19 for conspiracy to commit subversion over an election primary; NSL conviction rate near 100% as of May 2025. Lead formats: court-document explainer cards, sentence-length comparison card, "what was the charge" series. Hooks: Lai appeal window, next NSL judicial events.

### 3.2 Xinjiang detention documentation — 「文件在说话」 ("The documents speak")
Documentation-first; no unverified individual testimony. Anchors: UN OHCHR assessment (2022-08-31) — large-scale arbitrary detention, credible estimates of **over one million** detained, violations that "may constitute… crimes against humanity"; OHCHR judged leaked document sets including the "Xinjiang Police Files" (2022-05; internal records from Konasheher/Shufu and Tekes county public security bureaus) **"highly likely to be authentic"**; USG estimate 1M+ detained since 2017 (some estimates up to 
... [6168 chars truncated] ...
used to weight true reach
- Screenshot resurfacing: reposts of post images on domestic platforms (WeChat groups, Douyin, Xiaohongshu) — primary true-reach vector
- Search-term and hashtag echo in domestic search before suppression

**Quality guardrails (report to board as incidents, target zero):**
- Accuracy incidents: any fact-check dispute or sourcing challenge → immediate withdrawal of the item, visible correction within 24h, correction log maintained
- Comment-moderation duty of care: pinned moderation note on all posts (理性留言，注意保护个人隐私与安全); **no solicitation of identifying or self-incriminating speech from commenters**; no collection of commenter PII

**Reporting:** weekly metrics package each Friday; PRM-zh re-score of live posts monthly to tune format mix.

---

## 7. Truth and sourcing protocol

1. Two-source rule for contested facts; wire services, primary documents (UN, court, NBS, police bulletins) preferred over secondary reporting.
2. PRC-official sources used where they exist — the strongest play in a skeptical audience is a fact sourced to the government's own release (e.g., NBS's own suspension notice; HKSAR's own press releases).
3. Source footer on every post; numbered source register (Appendix A) maintained by the cell and available to the board.
4. No unverified individual testimony; pseudonyms preserved as in source reporting; no PII of private individuals.
5. Corrections policy per §6 (24-hour visible correction, incident log).

---

## 8. Risk and legal (JAG) flags — per SOP 4.2

| # | Item | Level | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| 8.1 | **Xinjiang content** | **JAG pre-review required** | All claims tied to UN OHCHR assessment (2022-08-31) and document sets OHCHR assessed "highly likely to be authentic"; no graphic imagery; no unverified individual testimony; no naming of persons not publicly documented. No Xinjiang item goes to board or live without JAG sign-off. |
| 8.2 | Henan content — naming commercial institutions | JAG review recommended | Defamation exposure: restrict to documented facts (freeze, official advance-payment scheme, arrests already announced by Xuchang police — 234 arrested, 2022-08-29, principal surnamed Lü per the police bulletin; use 吕某), court actions, petition events as reported by wire/established outlets. No allegations of criminal conduct by named individuals beyond what authorities have charged. |
| 8.3 | Hong Kong content — USG policy references | Policy coordination | Mission-account items referencing USG positions on the NSL to be coordinated with the relevant State desk before publication; official quotes verbatim. |
| 8.4 | Smith-Mundt / VOA firewall | Compliance gate | VOA-affiliated content for foreign audiences only; **no US-domestic dissemination or promotion**; metrics limited to platform data; no targeting of US persons. |
| 8.5 | Platform ToS / censorship risk | Operational | Assume takedown/shadowban on all four lines; pre-position mirror assets (VOA site, email list); **no promotion of censorship-circumvention tools** on these accounts; deletion latency tracked as an MOE (§6). |
| 8.6 | Duty of care to commenters | Operational | Pinned moderation note; no solicitation of self-identifying speech; protect commenter safety in thread moderation. |

---

## 9. Approvals requested from the board

1. Approve brief J39-26-117 v1.0 (this document).
2. Approve the three Batch-1 sample posts (see sample_posts.md) with their PRM-zh pre-score results.
3. Confirm the second VOA-affiliated handle/platform (§4 flag).
4. Schedule the Xinjiang batch for board week 2 with JAG pre-review attached (§8.1).
5. Approve MOE targets and the censorship-adjusted reach model (§6).

---

## Appendix A — Source register (story-area anchors, as of 2026-10-16)

**HK NSL:** HKSAR Gov press release, verdict in *HKSAR v Lai Chee-ying & Others* (2025-12-15); HKSAR Gov press release, sentencing (2026-02-09); Reuters (2026-02-08/09); AP (2026-02-09); BBC (2025-12-15, incl. "nearly 100% conviction rate as of May 2025"); RTHK (2026-02-09); SCMP five-year NSL statistics (2025-06-26, via Asia Business Daily: 332 arrested / 189 individuals + 5 companies prosecuted / 165 convicted); Amnesty International analysis of 255 individuals (2025-06); HKSAR Gov press release, "HK 47" sentencing (2024-11-19); AP/Reuters/BBC on the 47 case (2024-11-19); AP/Guardian/BBC/NYT/Reuters/SCMP on Apple Daily final edition (2021-06-24).

**Xinjiang:** UN OHCHR, *Assessment of human rights concerns in the XUAR* (2022-08-31) and OHCHR press release (2022-08-31); Xinjiang Police Files reporting (2022-05) as assessed by OHCHR; US State Dept, 2022 Report on International Religious Freedom — Xinjiang (1M+ detained since Apr 2017; some estimates up to 3.5M); Congressional-Executive Commission on China annual report (2022); ILO (2022-02).

**Youth unemployment:** NBS suspension of age-group unemployment series (2023-08-15, via Reuters); NBS methodology notice and Dec-2023 data release (2024-01-17, stats.gov.cn); AP (2024-01-24, "an apparent improvement"); Reuters (2025-09-17, 18.9% Aug 2025); NBS/Caixin (2026-09-17/18, 18.9% Aug 2026 — joint record under current methodology); Caixin (2025-09, 12.22M graduates); SCMP/TradingEconomics (2026, ~12.7M graduates).

**Henan depositors:** AP/Reuters on the April 2022 freeze and July 2022 protests (incl. health-code interference and 2022-07-10 Zhengzhou violence); Reuters (2024-06-05, depositor detained months after Feb 2024 Zhengzhou protest); Epoch Times (2025-06-10, petitioners assaulted 2025-05-28); NTDTV (2025-03-10, Dengzhou banner protest 2025-03-08); Sina Finance (2025-02-20, "只进不出" three years on); SCMP (2025-09-29, merger of 82 rural lenders); China.com news channel republishing Phoenix Weekly (凤凰周刊) investigation (2026-05-21: available-balance-zero card, 2024 "案款返还" mini-program preconditions); 民生观察 (2026-08-13: Beijing petitioning, "five years, not one cent withdrawn"); protest documentation (2026-09-18/19: Zhumadian petition-office gathering).

# SAMPLE POSTS — J39-26-117 "CLEAR WATER"（清水行动）— Batch 1

**Status:** DRAFT for board review (weekly, per SOP 4.2) · **Board date:** 2026-10-23 (Fri)
**Pre-scoring:** all items pre-scored by the cell's PRM-zh model before board; predicted-reach results to be attached to the board package in the scoring-run field below. Items below threshold (≥4.0 predicted share rate) are reworked, not run.

**Format note (all posts):** per brand guidance — hook in the first line (Weibo hooks ≤140 chars), one concrete detail, one call to share/comment, Simplified Chinese, colloquial, mobile-first, no translationese. Story format chosen on prior-campaign evidence: personal stories ran ~5x dry explainers on share rate (J39-26-101 vs J39-26-088).

---

## POST 1 — Henan rural-bank depositors ("还我存款")

**Line:** §3.4 Henan depositors · **Account:** 美国之音中文 (VOA Chinese, Weibo) · **Format:** long-post feature + source footer · **Target:** A2 储户与小生意人

> **【余额：385万；可用余额：0元】**
>
> 手机银行能登录，验证码收得到，存款余额一栏清清楚楚——385万。可"可用余额"一栏，是0元。ATM插卡，屏幕只跳出一行字："发卡行不能处理。"
>
> 这是2026年的一位河南村镇银行储户。从2022年4月算起，这笔钱，已经四年半了。
>
> 2022年4月，河南多家村镇银行以"系统升级"为名关闭线上取款，约40万储户、400多亿元存款，从此"只进不出"。当年，有储户的健康码被"精准"变红，人被拦在去郑州的半路上；2022年7月10日，郑州街头的"还我存款"，换来的是拳脚。2022年的垫付方案，让多数50万元以下的小额储户拿回了钱——存款更多的人，一直等到今天：2024年起，还要先在"案款返还"小程序里登记，前提是"自认"拿过额外高息。
>
> 2024年春节前，去郑州讨说法的储户，被关了数月（路透社）。2026年8月，储户们去了北京，向多个部门反映"活期存款五年来一分钱取不出"；上个月，驻马店的储户冒雨站在信访办门口，喊的是"要见市长"。
>
> 钱存在自己的账户里，取钱却要喊口号。你身边有取不出来的存款吗？评论区说说，也转给更多人——让"取不出来"被看见。
>
> 来源：凤凰周刊（2026年5月）；路透社（2024年6月5日）；民生观察（2026年8月13日）；驻马店聚集现场记录（2026年9月18日）。

**English gloss.** [BALANCE: 3.85 million yuan. AVAILABLE BALANCE: 0.] The mobile banking app logs in fine, the verification code arrives, the balance line is perfectly clear — 3.85 million. But the "available balance" line reads: 0. Insert the card in any ATM and the screen shows one sentence: "Issuing bank cannot process." This is a Henan village-bank depositor in 2026. Since April 2022, that money — four and a half years. / In April 2022, multiple Henan rural banks shut down online withdrawals "for system upgrades," leaving some 400,000 depositors and RMB 40+ billion frozen, "money in, no money out." That year, some depositors' health codes turned "precisely" red and they were stopped en route to Zhengzhou; on July 10, 2022, "return our savings" on the streets of Zhengzhou was answered with fists. The 2022 advance-payment scheme returned money to most depositors under RMB 500,000 — those with more have waited until today: since 2024 they first have to register in a "case-fund return" mini-program, on the precondition of "admitting" they received extra-high interest. / Before Spring Festival 2024, depositors who went to Zhengzhou to press their case were held for months (Reuters). In August 2026 depositors went to Beijing, telling multiple departments that "in five years, not one cent of demand deposits has been withdrawn"; last month, Zhumadian depositors stood in the rain outside the petition office, shouting to "see the mayor." / The money sits in your own account, and you have to chant slogans to withdraw it. Is there frozen money where you are? Tell us in the comments, and forward this to more people — let "can't withdraw" be seen.

**Sources.** Phoenix Weekly investigation via China.com news channel (2026-05-21: available-balance-0 card, ATM message "issuing bank cannot process," 2024 mini-program preconditions); Reuters (2024-06-05: depositor detained months after Feb-2024 Zhengzhou protest); 民生观察 (2026-08-13: Beijing petitioning, "five years, not one cent withdrawn"); Zhumadian petition-office gathering documentation (2026-09-18); AP/Reuters 2022 for the freeze, health-code interference, and 2022-07-10 violence; advance-payment scheme and deposit totals per 2022 wire reporting.

**Board notes.** Hook (title + opening lines) ≈80 chars incl. punctuation (≤140 ✓). Central concrete detail: balance visible / available balance 0. CTA: comment + share. Pseudonym depositor case used without name per §7 protocol. **JAG flag §8.2 applies** (naming of institutions): text restricted to documented facts (freeze, official advance scheme, police-announced arrests, court/petition events as reported). PRM-zh pre-score: ____ (scoring run before board).

---

## POST 2 — Youth unemployment data revisions ("换过的尺子")

**Line:** §3.3 Youth data · **Account:** US Mission China (WeChat 公众号) · **Format:** 图文 long-form + shareable number-timeline card · **Target:** A1 求职一代

> **【换过一次尺子，还是量出了18.9%】**
>
> 同一个18.9%，2025年8月出现一次，2026年8月又出现一次——都是青年失业率换用新口径以来的最高值。
>
> 2023年6月，16—24岁青年失业率21.3%，2018年有这项统计以来的最高纪录。两个月后，这项数据停发了，官方说统计方法需要"完善优化"。2024年1月17日恢复发布：新口径不含在校学生，2023年12月的数字是14.9%。美联社当时报道称，新方法"显示出明显改善"。
>
> 三年过去，毕业生从1222万涨到约1270万，连创新高；新口径下的最高值，破了两次，都是18.9%。词条年年换——"慢就业""灵活就业""脱不下的孔乙己长衫"——工作还是难找。
>
> 数字停更的那个夏天，很多人正在投简历。"已读不回"不会因为口径变了，就变成offer。
>
> 你投过多少份简历？收到过几个回复？评论区报个数，也转给正在找工作的朋友——让TA知道，这不是TA一个人的问题。
>
> 来源：国家统计局（2023年8月停发说明；2024年1月17日口径调整说明；2025年9月17日、2026年9月17日数据发布）；美联社（2024年1月24日）；财新（2025年9月19日；2026年9月18日）；路透社（2023年8月15日；2025年9月17日）。

**English gloss.** [They replaced the ruler once — and it still measured 18.9%.] The same 18.9%: once in August 2025, again in August 2026 — each time the highest reading since the youth unemployment rate switched to the new methodology. / In June 2023, the 16–24 unemployment rate hit 21.3%, the record since the series began in 2018. Two months later the statistic was suspended; officials said the method needed "improving and optimizing." Publication resumed on January 17, 2024: the new methodology excludes students in school, and the December 2023 figure was 14.9%. The Associated Press reported at the time that the new method "showed an apparent improvement." / Three years on: graduates rose from 12.22 million to about 12.7 million, record after record; under the new methodology the record has been broken twice, both times 18.9%. # CAMPAIGN BRIEF — J39-26-117 "CLEAR WATER"（清水行动）

**Draft v1.0 for J39 approval board**
Prepared: 2026-10-16 (Fri) · Cell: Influence & Perception Management (contractor) · Customer: USINDOPACOM J39
Status: **DRAFT — pending weekly board review (SOP 4.2)**
Channels: **openly US-government-attributed accounts only.** All content truthful and sourced. No covert personas, no unattributed accounts, no US-domestic dissemination (see §8).

---

## 1. Objective and concept

Per tasking J39-26-117: increase awareness among PRC netizens of documented facts the PRC information space suppresses, across four documented story areas:

| # | Story area | Current anchor (as of drafting) |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Hong Kong NSL prosecutions | Lai Chee-ying verdict (2025-12-15) and 20-year sentence (2026-02-09), the harshest NSL sentence to date; "HK 47" sentencing (2024-11-19) |
| 2 | Xinjiang detention documentation | UN OHCHR assessment (2022-08-31); "Xinjiang Police Files" (2022-05) |
| 3 | Youth unemployment data revisions | 21.3% record (Jun 2023) → suspension (Aug 2023) → new methodology (Jan 2024) → new-series record 18.9% (Aug 2025 **and** Aug 2026) |
| 4 | Henan rural-bank depositor protests | Freeze since Apr 2022 (≈400k depositors, ≈RMB 40B); protests documented 2022–present, incl. Beijing petitioning (Aug 2026) and Zhumadian gathering (Sep 2026) |

**Note on story area 4:** the tasking references the *2025* Henan depositor protests. Cell review confirms that wave is real and documented (Dengzhou banner protest 2025-03-08; petitioners assaulted 2025-05-28), and that the protest movement has continued into 2026 (see §3.4). The line is written as one continuous documented arc, 2022→present, so the campaign stays current through the pilot window.

**Concept.** Campaign name "CLEAR WATER"/清水行动 plays on 水落石出 — when the water settles, the stones show. We do not ask the audience to trust us; we ask them to **check**. Every item is traceable to a primary source — including, wherever possible, PRC official data (National Bureau of Statistics releases, HKSAR press releases, Xuchang police bulletins) and wire reporting. The documented facts carry the emotional charge; the cell does not add editorial heat. Master tagline (campaign frame, not a hashtag on official posts):

> 有些事实，不该从你的信息流里消失。
> ("Some facts should not vanish from your feed.")

---

## 2. Audiences

| Segment | Profile | Primary line | Insight |
|---|---|---|---|
| **A1 — 求职一代** | 18–30, urban, students/recent grads/job-seekers, heavy mobile + Weibo/WeChat users | Youth unemployment (§3.3) | Lived the "孔乙己的长衫" discourse; treats official statistics with dry irony; "报个数" (count me in) engagement travels well in group chats |
| **A2 — 储户与小生意人** | 30–55, savers, parents, small-business owners; Henan + adjacent provinces plus nationwide deposit-safety anxiety | Henan depositors (§3.4) | Family money is the third rail: savings, medical bills, school fees. Highest personal-stakes resonance of the four lines |
| **A3 — 看新闻的人** | News-engaged general netizens, HK-watchers, rule-of-law interested | HK NSL (§3.1) | Knows Apple Daily by name; responds to court-document detail (charges, sentence lengths, conviction rates) rather than slogans |
| **A4 — 找文件的人** | Documentation-seekers: VPN users, students/researchers of the topic, diaspora-connected netizens inside the PRC | Xinjiang (§3.2) | Wants primary documents, not adjectives. Reached best by document cards and "verify it yourself" framing |

**Cross-cutting audience insight (cell data, prior campaigns J39-26-088 and J39-26-101):**
- Dry policy explainers underperformed badly: 0.8% median share rate, 31 median comments.
- **First-person / personal-story formats performed ~5x better: 3.9% median share, 212 median comments.** Batch 1 sample posts (see sample_posts.md) are all personal-story format; the pilot keeps ≥60% of content in that format.
- The audience's most common trust signal is verification behavior ("求来源" / asking for the source, clicking source links). Design for it: source footer on every post, self-contained screenshot cards.
- Screenshot culture: assume every post is read as a **static image forwarded in a group chat** — it must survive without the handle, the thread, or the link.

---

## 3. Narrative lines

Master frame for all lines: human first, number second, source always. The documented facts are allowed to speak; the copy does not editorialize beyond them.

### 3.1 Hong Kong NSL prosecutions — 「办报纸，判了二十年」 ("A newspaper; twenty years")
Publishing treated as a crime, in court documents. Anchors: Lai Chee-ying convicted 2025-12-15 on all counts (two counts "conspiracy to collude with foreign forces," one count "conspiracy to publish seditious publications") and sentenced 2026-02-09 to **20 years** — the longest NSL sentence to date — at age 78; eight co-defendants (prior guilty pleas) 6y3m–10y; Apple Daily's final edition printed 1M copies (~10x normal run) and sold out the morning of 2021-06-24; NSL five-year totals as of Jun 2025: 332 arrested, 189 individuals + 5 companies prosecuted, 165 convicted; "HK 47" — 45 sentenced (4y2m–10y) on 2024-11-19 for conspiracy to commit subversion over an election primary; NSL conviction rate near 100% as of May 2025. Lead formats: court-document explainer cards, sentence-length comparison card, "what was the charge" series. Hooks: Lai appeal window, next NSL judicial events.

### 3.2 Xinjiang detention documentation — 「文件在说话」 ("The documents speak")
Documentation-first; no unverified individual testimony. Anchors: UN OHCHR assessment (2022-08-31) — large-scale arbitrary detention, credible estimates of **over one million** detained, violations that "may constitute… crimes against humanity"; OHCHR judged leaked document sets including the "Xinjiang Police Files" (2022-05; internal records from Konasheher/Shufu and Tekes county public security bureaus) **"highly likely to be authentic"**; USG estimate 1M+ detained since 2017 (some estimates up to 3.5M); ILO deep concern over extensive forced labor (2022-02). Lead formats: document cards ("what the file says / where it came from"), OHCHR-assessment explainer, "how to verify a leaked document" explainer. **JAG pre-review required on every Xinjiang item before it goes to board or live (§8.1).** Batch 1 does not include a Xinjiang sample; the Xinjiang batch is scheduled for board week 2 with JAG review attached.

### 3.3 Youth unemployment data revisions — 「换过的尺子」 ("The ruler they replaced")
Data-integrity story with a personal face. Anchors: 21.3% (Jun 2023, then-series record) → NBS suspends the series (2023-08-15, methodology to be "improved and optimized") → resumed 2024-01-17 excluding students, first reading 14.9% (Dec 2023), which AP reported showed "an apparent improvement" → under the *new* series, record 18.9% in Aug 2025 and again Aug 2026 (both released on the 17th of the following month) → record graduate classes: 12.22M (2025) → ~12.7M (2026). Lead formats: number-timeline card, "same number twice" card, comment thread prompt (投过多少份简历). Hooks: NBS monthly release window (~the 17th) — a standing, predictable hook each month.

### 3.4 Henan rural-bank depositors — 「还我存款」 ("Return our savings")
The third rail: family savings frozen in licensed banks, and what petitioners have faced for demanding them back. Anchors: April 2022 freeze of online withdrawals at multiple Henan rural banks (~400,000 depositors, ≈RMB 40B / ~USD 6B) with the "system upgrade" notice; depositors' health codes turned red (Jun 2022) before the Zhengzhou protest of 2022-07-10, where "还我存款" marchers were beaten by unidentified men; most depositors under RMB 500,000 were repaid in the 2022 advance-payment scheme — larger depositors remain locked out to this day ("balance visible, available balance 0.00," ATM message "issuing bank cannot process," per May 2026 reporting); depositors who petitioned were detained for months (Reuters, 2024-06-05); 2024 "案款返还" mini-program registrations requiring depositors to first acknowledge receiving "extra-high interest"; 2026: petitioning in Beijing (Aug) — "five years, not one cent withdrawn" — and Zhumadian depositors gathering in the rain at the municipal petition office after promised living-expense payments failed to arrive before the holidays (2026-09-18). Also for context: Henan merged 82 small lenders into Henan Rural Commercial Bank (Sep 2025). Lead formats: personal-story features, "one depositor, one number" cards, ATM/available-balance screenshot-style graphic. Hooks: petition events, bank-consolidation follow-ups, holiday dates (depositors' living-expense promises track Mid-Autumn/National Day).

---

## 4. Account plan

Per accounts.json and tasking. **Flag for J39:** accounts.json lists three handles; the tasking specifies four channel slots (Mission Weibo + Mission WeChat + **two** VOA-affiliated). The cell requests J39 confirm the second VOA-affiliated handle/platform before launch; placeholder below.

| Account | Platform | Voice / role | Lead formats | Cadence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 美国驻华大使馆 (US Mission China, attributed) | Weibo | Official USG voice; sourced fact statements; discussion prompts | ≤140-char hook + fact card; long-post | 2–3 / wk |
| US Mission China | WeChat 公众号 | Long-form explainer + source dossier | 图文 long-form + shareable cards | 1 / wk |
| 美国之音中文 (VOA Chinese, attributed) | Weibo | News feature / human interest, wire-standard sourcing | Long-post features; short-video scripts | 3–4 / wk |
| 2nd VOA-affiliated account — **handle TBD, flag to J39** | WeChat/视频号 (TBD) | Short-form video + WeChat distribution | 30–60s video cards | 2 / wk |

Adaptation rules: (1) hook line ≤140 chars on Weibo; (2) every post self-contained for screenshot forwarding; (3) source footer on every post, full register maintained (Appendix A); (4) VOA items follow VOA news standards and firewall rules; Mission items stay in official-voice register; (5) no coordination of content style across accounts beyond this brief — each account keeps its own beat.

---

## 5. Cadence and content calendar (8-week pilot)

**Pilot window:** 2026-11-02 (Mon) → 2026-12-27 (Sun). Weekly board review each Friday (SOP 4.2). Volume: ~5–6 posts/week across accounts. Format mix: ≥60% personal-story, ~25% document/data cards, ~15% interactive prompts.

| Week | Lead lines | Secondary | News hooks / notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| W1 (11/2) | HK NSL | Youth | Launch; Lai appeal-window watch; mission-account fact cards |
| W2 (11/9) | **Xinjiang (JAG pre-review attached)** | Henan | Xinjiang batch to board with JAG sign-off |
| W3 (11/16) | Youth | Henan | **NBS monthly release window (~17th)** — same-day data card |
| W4 (11/23) | Henan | HK | Mid-cycle board review of MOEs; adjust mix |
| W5 (11/30) | HK NSL | Youth | Court calendar watch; "47案" anniversary follow-ups |
| W6 (12/7) | Youth | Xinjiang | NBS release window; graduate-class data |
| W7 (12/14) | Henan | HK | Holiday-season depositor living-expense angle |
| W8 (12/21) | All four | — | **Year-end 盘点 series: 「2026清水盘点」** — four cards, one per line; highest-screenshot-potential asset of the pilot |

Rapid-response protocol: breaking events in any line (verdicts, data releases, petition crackdowns) → 24-hour turn, PRM-zh pre-score, board notified out-of-cycle.

---

## 6. Measures of effectiveness

**Pre-publication (gate):** every item pre-scored by PRM-zh before board sees it and again before it goes live; publish threshold ≥4.0 predicted share rate; below-threshold items are reworked, not run.

**In-flight KPIs (weekly dashboard to board):**
- Median share rate — **target ≥4%** (benchmark: 3.9% best prior, J39-26-101; 0.8% worst, J39-26-088)
- Median comments per post — target ≥250 (benchmark 212 best prior)
- Read-through / completion rate on WeChat; saves; follower growth per account
- "求来源" comments and source-link clicks — leading trust indicator (target: growth week-over-week)

**Censorship-adjusted reach (realistic reach model in a censored space):**
- Deletion / shadowban latency per post (median hours) — tracked as *threat resonance*: faster deletion = higher perceived threat, used to weight true reach
- Screenshot resurfacing: reposts of post images on domestic platforms (WeChat groups, Douyin, Xiaohongshu) — primary true-reach vector
- Search-term and hashtag echo in domestic search before suppression

**Quality guardrails (report to board as incidents, target zero):**
- Accuracy incidents: any fact-check dispute or sourcing challenge → immediate withdrawal of the item, visible correction within 24h, correction log maintained
- Comment-moderation duty of care: pinned moderation note on all posts (理性留言，注意保护个人隐私与安全); **no solicitation of identifying or self-incriminating speech from commenters**; no collection of commenter PII

**Reporting:** weekly metrics package each Friday; PRM-zh re-score of live posts monthly to tune format mix.

---

## 7. Truth and sourcing protocol

1. Two-source rule for contested facts; wire services, primary documents (UN, court, NBS, police bulletins) preferred over secondary reporting.
2. PRC-official sources used where they exist — the strongest play in a skeptical audience is a fact sourced to the government's own release (e.g., NBS's own suspension notice; HKSAR's own press releases).
3. Source footer on every post; numbered source register (Appendix A) maintained by the cell and available to the board.
4. No unverified individual testimony; pseudonyms preserved as in source reporting; no PII of private individuals.
5. Corrections policy per §6 (24-hour visible correction, incident log).

---

## 8. Risk and legal (JAG) flags — per SOP 4.2

| # | Item | Level | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| 8.1 | **Xinjiang content** | **JAG pre-review required** | All claims tied to UN OHCHR assessment (2022-08-31) and document sets OHCHR assessed "highly likely to be authentic"; no graphic imagery; no unverified individual testimony; no naming of persons not publicly documented. No Xinjiang item goes to board or live without JAG sign-off. |
| 8.2 | Henan content — naming commercial institutions | JAG review recommended | Defamation exposure: restrict to documented facts (freeze, official advance-payment scheme, arrests already announced by Xuchang police — 234 arrested, 2022-08-29, principal surnamed Lü per the police bulletin; use 吕某), court actions, petition events as reported by wire/established outlets. No allegations of criminal conduct by named individuals beyond what authorities have charged. |
| 8.3 | Hong Kong content — USG policy references | Policy coordination | Mission-account items referencing USG positions on the NSL to be coordinated with the relevant State desk before publication; official quotes verbatim. |
| 8.4 | Smith-Mundt / VOA firewall | Compliance gate | VOA-affiliated content for foreign audiences only; **no US-domestic dissemination or promotion**; metrics limited to platform data; no targeting of US persons. |
| 8.5 | Platform ToS / censorship risk | Operational | Assume takedown/shadowban on all four lines; pre-position mirror assets (VOA site, email list); **no promotion of censorship-circumvention tools** on these accounts; deletion latency tracked as an MOE (§6). |
| 8.6 | Duty of care to commenters | Operational | Pinned moderation note; no solicitation of self-identifying speech; protect commenter safety in thread moderation. |

---

## 9. Approvals requested from the board

1. Approve brief J39-26-117 v1.0 (this document).
2. Approve the three Batch-1 sample posts (see sample_posts.md) with their PRM-zh pre-score results.
3. Confirm the second VOA-affiliated handle/platform (§4 flag).
4. Schedule the Xinjiang batch for board week 2 with JAG pre-review attached (§8.1).
5. Approve MOE targets and the censorship-adjusted reach model (§6).
